title: No signal or no service
content:
If your phone shows 'No Service', 'No Signal', or 'Emergency Calls Only', follow these steps in order:

1. Check if your SIM is properly inserted. Power off your phone, remove the SIM tray, and reseat the SIM card. Make sure it clicks into place. Power the phone back on and wait up to 2 minutes for network registration.

2. Toggle Airplane Mode. Turn Airplane Mode on, wait 10 seconds, then turn it off. This forces your phone to re-scan for networks.

3. Manually select the network. Go to Settings > Mobile Network > Network Operators > Search Networks. Wait for the list to populate (this can take 30-60 seconds). Select 'ACME' or 'ACME PH' from the list. If ACME does not appear, your area may not have coverage — check the coverage map at airgap.dev/coverage.

4. Check for network outages. Open the ACME app (on WiFi) or visit airgap.dev/status to see if there is a known outage in your area.

5. Check your SIM status. Dial *123# — if it does not connect, your SIM may be deactivated. Possible reasons: expired prepaid SIM (no load for 180+ days), unpaid postpaid bill (3+ months overdue), or SIM registration not completed under RA 11934.

6. Test with another phone. Insert your ACME SIM into a different phone. If it works in the other phone, the issue is with your original device (hardware or settings). If it still shows no service, the SIM itself may be damaged.

7. Check if your phone supports ACME bands. ACME uses 4G LTE Bands 1, 3, 7, 28 and 5G n78. Some imported or very old phones may not support these frequencies. Verify at airgap.dev/devices.

8. Reset network settings. On iOS: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset > Reset > Reset Network Settings. On Android: Settings > General Management > Reset > Reset Network Settings. Warning: this erases saved WiFi passwords.

9. Check for a carrier settings update. On iOS: Settings > General > About — if an update is available, a prompt will appear. On Android, carrier settings update automatically.

10. If none of the above works, visit a ACME store for a free SIM diagnostic. Bring your phone and a valid ID. The issue may require a SIM replacement (PHP 50) or a device inspection.

title: Slow mobile data or internet
content:
If your mobile data is slower than expected, follow these diagnostic steps:

1. Run a speed test. Open the ACME app > Tools > Speed Test, or visit speedtest.airgap.dev. Run the test 3 times at different moments. Expected speeds: 4G LTE: 20-75 Mbps. 5G: 100-500 Mbps. If your speed is below 5 Mbps on 4G, there is likely an issue.

2. Check your data allocation. Dial *123*3# or check the ACME app under Account > Data Usage. If you have consumed all your data, prepaid users will have no data access, and postpaid users are throttled to 256 Kbps. Buy a data add-on to restore full speed.

3. Check your signal strength. Look at the signal bars on your phone. One or two bars indicates weak signal which directly impacts speed. Try moving to an open area, near a window, or to a higher floor. Walls, buildings, and underground locations weaken signal.

4. Check if you are on 4G or 3G. Go to Settings > Mobile Network and verify your network mode is set to '4G/LTE' or 'Auto'. If your phone is stuck on 3G or 2G, speeds will be significantly lower. Set it to 'LTE/4G preferred' or '5G/LTE/3G/2G (Auto)'.

5. Toggle mobile data off and on. Settings > Mobile Data > toggle off, wait 5 seconds, toggle on. This forces a fresh data connection.

6. Clear your phone's DNS cache. Open your browser and clear browsing data/cache. Alternatively, switch to a public DNS: Settings > WiFi > Advanced > DNS > enter 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1.

7. Check for background app usage. Some apps consume large amounts of data in the background (cloud backups, video auto-play, app updates). On iOS: Settings > Cellular > scroll down to see per-app usage. On Android: Settings > Data Usage > App Data Usage. Disable background data for heavy consumers.

8. Check network congestion. Mobile speeds are slower during peak hours (12PM-2PM and 6PM-10PM) in dense urban areas. If your tests during off-peak hours show normal speeds, congestion is the cause. Consider using WiFi during peak times.

9. Verify APN settings. Incorrect APN settings can cause slow or no data. See the APN configuration guide for correct settings. The correct ACME APN is 'airgap.internet'.

10. Restart your phone. A simple restart clears temporary network glitches and refreshes your connection to the nearest cell tower.

11. If speeds remain consistently below expected levels in an area with good coverage, report it via the ACME app under Support > Report Network Issue, or call 123. Include your location, time of day, and speed test results so the network team can investigate.

title: Cannot connect to WiFi (ACME Fiber)
content:
If you cannot connect to your ACME Fiber WiFi or your connection keeps dropping, follow these steps:

1. Check the router lights. A healthy ACME router shows: Power (solid green), Internet/WAN (solid green), WiFi (blinking green). If the Power light is off, check the power cable and outlet. If the Internet/WAN light is off or red, the fiber connection to your home may be down — skip to step 7.

2. Restart the router. Unplug the power cable from the router (and the ONT/modem if separate), wait 30 seconds, plug the ONT back in first, wait for it to fully boot (all lights stable, about 2 minutes), then plug in the router. Wait another 2 minutes for WiFi to broadcast.

3. Check if the issue is WiFi or internet. Connect a device directly to the router using an ethernet cable. If wired internet works but WiFi does not, the issue is WiFi-specific. If wired also does not work, the issue is your internet connection.

4. Forget and reconnect to WiFi. On your device, go to WiFi settings, find your ACME network, select 'Forget This Network', then reconnect by entering the password. The default password is printed on a sticker under the router. If you changed it, use your custom password.

5. Check for WiFi interference. Move the router to a central, elevated location away from walls, microwaves, cordless phones, and other electronics. Avoid placing the router inside a cabinet. If you have many devices, try connecting to the 5GHz band (usually named 'YourNetwork_5G') for faster speeds in close range, or the 2.4GHz band for better range through walls.

6. Check the number of connected devices. Log in to the router admin panel at 192.168.1.1 (default login: admin / airgap2024) and check the connected devices list. The standard ACME router supports up to 32 simultaneous WiFi connections. Too many devices can slow everyone down.

7. Inspect the fiber cable. The fiber optic cable runs from outside your home to the ONT box. Check for any visible damage, sharp bends (fiber cables should not be bent more than 90 degrees), or disconnected connectors. Do not attempt to repair fiber cables yourself — call 123 for a technician visit.

8. Check for area outages. Visit airgap.dev/status or the ACME app for service status. If there is a known outage in your area, wait for it to be resolved.

9. Factory reset the router (last resort). Press and hold the reset button on the back of the router with a pin for 10 seconds until all lights blink. The router will restart with factory defaults. You will need to reconnect all your devices using the default WiFi name and password from the sticker. Custom settings (port forwarding, parental controls) will be lost.

10. If the issue persists, call 123 and select the Fiber Support option. A remote diagnostic can check your line quality. If a technician visit is needed, it will be scheduled within 2 business days (free for issues covered by the service agreement).

title: APN settings configuration (Android and iOS)
content:
If your mobile data is not working, your APN (Access Point Name) settings may be incorrect. Here is how to configure them for ACME:

Correct ACME APN settings:
- Name: ACME Internet
- APN: airgap.internet
- Proxy: (leave blank)
- Port: (leave blank)
- Username: (leave blank)
- Password: (leave blank)
- Server: (leave blank)
- MMSC: http://mms.airgap.dev
- MMS Proxy: 10.102.61.46
- MMS Port: 8080
- MCC: 515
- MNC: 05
- Authentication Type: None
- APN Type: default,mms,supl
- APN Protocol: IPv4/IPv6
- APN Roaming Protocol: IPv4
- Bearer: Unspecified

For Android:
1. Go to Settings > Connections (or Network & Internet) > Mobile Networks > Access Point Names.
2. If a ACME APN already exists, tap it and verify all fields match the settings above.
3. If no ACME APN exists, tap the '+' or 'Add' button to create a new APN.
4. Enter all the fields listed above.
5. Tap the three-dot menu (or Save) to save the APN.
6. Select the new ACME APN as the active APN (tap the radio button next to it).
7. Restart your phone.

For iOS (iPhone):
iPhones typically configure APN settings automatically via carrier settings updates. If data is not working:
1. Go to Settings > General > About. If a carrier settings update is available, install it.
2. If data still does not work, go to Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Network.
3. Under 'Cellular Data', set APN to: airgap.internet (leave username and password blank).
4. Under 'MMS', set APN to: airgap.internet, MMSC to: http://mms.airgap.dev, MMS Proxy to: 10.102.61.46:8080.
5. Restart your phone.

Note: If the Cellular Data Network option is not visible on your iPhone, it means carrier settings are locked. Reset network settings (Settings > General > Transfer or Reset > Reset > Reset Network Settings) and check for a carrier settings update again.

After configuring APN:
- Toggle Airplane Mode on and off.
- Verify data works by opening a website.
- If data works but MMS does not, double-check the MMS-specific fields.
- If issues persist, call 123 — a support agent can send an automatic APN configuration to your phone via SMS.

title: SIM registration issues
content:
If you are having trouble registering your SIM card under RA 11934 (Philippine SIM Registration Act), follow these steps:

1. Check registration status. Dial *888*9# or visit airgap.dev/simreg to check if your SIM is already registered, pending, or unregistered.

2. Common registration errors and solutions:

- 'Invalid ID': Make sure your ID is a government-issued photo ID. Accepted IDs: Philippine passport, driver's license, PhilSys/national ID, SSS ID, UMID, voter's ID, postal ID, PRC ID, senior citizen ID, PWD ID, OFW ID, or Alien Certificate of Registration. Student IDs and company IDs are not accepted.

- 'Selfie verification failed': Ensure you are in a well-lit area. Remove sunglasses, hats, or face masks. Hold your phone at eye level. Your face should fill most of the frame. Avoid backlighting (do not face a window). The system compares your selfie to your ID photo, so your appearance should reasonably match.

- 'ID photo unclear': Take a clear, flat photo of your ID. Avoid glare (do not use flash). All four corners of the ID must be visible. Text on the ID must be readable. File size must be under 10MB. Supported formats: JPG, PNG.

- 'Name mismatch': The name you enter must exactly match the name on your ID, including middle name or initial. If your ID has your name in all caps, you can enter it in regular case. Suffixes (Jr., III, etc.) must also match.

- 'Address not found': Use the complete address format including street, barangay, city/municipality, and province. If your address is not recognized in the auto-complete, try entering it manually without abbreviations.

- 'OTP not received': Wait at least 2 minutes. Check your SMS inbox (not spam/junk). Ensure your SIM has signal. If still not received, tap 'Resend OTP'. You can request up to 5 OTPs per hour.

- 'Registration portal down or slow': High traffic can slow the portal. Try during off-peak hours (6AM-9AM or after 9PM). The ACME app registration tends to be faster than the website.

3. Registration via ACME store. If online registration is not working, visit any ACME store with your valid ID. Store staff can complete your registration in-person using their dedicated system. This is the most reliable method if you are having repeated issues online.

4. Foreign nationals. Expats and foreign residents can register using their passport plus any of the following: ACR I-Card, Special Resident Retiree's Visa, or work visa/permit.

5. Minors (under 18). Registration must be done by a parent or legal guardian. The parent registers using their own ID and indicates the minor as the SIM user. Both the parent's and minor's information are recorded.

6. Timeline. After successful registration, confirmation is sent via SMS within 24 hours. If you do not receive confirmation after 48 hours, call 123 or visit a store to verify your registration status.

7. Consequences of non-registration. Unregistered SIMs may be deactivated as required by law. If your SIM is deactivated due to non-registration, visit a ACME store with your ID to re-register and reactivate (no fee, but this may take up to 24 hours).
